Title: Persist a bounded evidence projection so provenance works beyond the previous turn
Why: turn_memory has no evidence column and nothing writes the record to any durable store. Only the latest turn's record survives, in Redis, keyed by conversation with no turn index. Approach: ALTER TABLE turn_memory ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS evidence JSONB (a live DB needs its own ALTER - the DDL is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS). Approach: Add a same-tier disagreement state to the verdict and have describe() say it. Tiebreak only on evidence: an explicit supersedes link first, then the later effectiveFrom - never on arrival order.

Title: Put the authority tiers in the graph, generated from the policy file

Evidence: grep -i precedence over every TTL returns ONE rdfs:comment (ontosage_schema.ttl:2030). authorityTier: 0 hits anywhere. Register the new class as subClassOf o:Record or o:IntervalRecord AND give it o:layTerms, or record_registry's discovery will not see it (and see G1 for what a class with no bare lay term costs).

DEVIATED from the row's own suggestion to reuse ontosage:SourceType: that class already means something different in the live schema (WHICH LANE answered a question -- GraphDB/Analytics/FloorPlan/Document/...), confirmed by reading every existing instance in ontology/ontosage_schema.ttl. Reusing it would conflate 'what answered' with 'how authoritative was it'. VERIFIED LIVE end to end: generated, written, orchestrator restarted, ttl_uploader log confirms upload ('bldg1_source_precedence.ttl uploaded'), and a live SPARQL query against GraphDB correctly returns every kind at its right tier (booking/alarm/register/... -> authoritative rank 30; sensor -> measurement rank 20; human_report -> inference rank 10) -- 'which kind of record wins' now has real triples to answer from. tests/test_e5_precedence_tiers_are_in_the_graph.py 5/5, including one asserting the output tracks precedence.RANK's own values rather than a frozen copy.

Title: Populate supersedes and currencyThresholdDays WITH their readers in the same change
Why: Both are declared for exactly this purpose, carry zero triples, and have NO functional reader. Notes: 2026-10-07, owner decision (binding): TTL first, drawing second, none third. design_occupancy.authoritative_capacity() is the one place the order is decided: a TTL figure for the space wins; a drawing figure is read only when the TTL holds none; otherwise none. A drawing never joins a TTL tie. The drawing figures 30 / 7 / 8 stay as retained second-source records (ontosage:capacitySource "drawing") and answer nothing today, because every room that has a drawing also holds a TTL figure. The drawing no longer supersedes the estimate. ontosage:capacitySource is declared in ontology/ontosage_schema.ttl. NOT DONE, deliberately: currencyThresholdDays is not populated. The capacity records carry no effectiveFrom, so a currency reader would have no date to measure against, and the row's own rule says not to populate a property without its reader. Tests: tests/test_capacity_authority_order.py (new, 31 cases; the authority order on synthetic figures, the real TTL through the real reader, and a drawing-only space) -- 26 of them fail on the pre-E6 code; tests/test_capacity_drawing_and_authority.py updated (its pins were the 2026-10-06 order; the DXF evidence test is unchanged); tests/test_capacity_drawing_supersedes.py removed (its valid checks moved to the new file). Targeted run 145 passed, 3 xfailed; the design-occupancy, capacity and provisioning files all green. Title: P1 PRIVACY: stop every unrecognised tester sharing one memory partition
Why: Any request without a recognised forwarded email falls back to the identity 'openwebui_user', and cross-session memory retrieval filters on user_id. So tester B's classification prompt can be primed with tester A's question AND answer summary, figures included. This defeats the isolation tests/test_privacy_t40.py pins per user, and it is the one P1 in this plan.
Evidence: main.py:3076 fallback = ('openwebui_user','readonly'); :4000 sets user_id=username on /v1. Measured: Qdrant user_memory filtered on user_id=openwebui_user -> 1,742 points; turn_memory openwebui_user -> 1,702 rows (second only to facility01's 6,703). agent_memory.retrieve_context filters on user_id at :318-320.
Approach: Two parts. (1) Never write cross-session memory under a shared fallback identity: skip the store when the identity is the fallback. (2) Never retrieve under it either. Then quarantine the 1,742 existing points. The 60 registered trial accounts resolve to real identities, so this affects unregistered testers and every harness run.
Acceptance: A probe as two different unregistered emails shows no cross-contamination; tests/test_privacy_t40.py's isolation assertions hold on the /v1 path.
Notes: Part (1) and (2) of the plan's own Approach done: _orchestrator.py's cross-session memory WRITE (~line 7405, store_success) and READ (~line 2128, retrieve_context) both now require state.user_id != 'openwebui_user' -- main.py resolve_forwarded_user()'s own least-privilege fallback constant, matched by equality the way main.py:4010 already does. Source-pinned tests in tests/test_f3_f8_memory_hygiene.py (2 new, both verify the guard sits on the SAME if as the call, not just somewhere nearby) + the existing tests/test_privacy_t40.py and tests/test_phase_bc_services.py all green (58+17 passed) run fresh and standalone to avoid the tree-pinning risk of a long concurrent suite run. NOT done: part (3), quarantining the ~1,742 existing Qdrant points already stored under the shared identity. That is a live data-deletion action against production Qdrant and is being done as a separate, measured step (dry-run count first) rather than bundled into this code change. Part (3) also done: new scripts/quarantine_shared_identity_memory.py, dry-run by default, --delete to act, talks to Qdrant's REST API directly. Measured 1,745 points (vs the plan's 1,742 -- 3 more landed before the code fix went live) under 'openwebui_user' out of 26,671 total. Ran --delete: 0 remain, 24,926 under real identities confirmed untouched before and after (26,671 - 1,745 = 24,926 exactly).

Title: Redact figures from cross-session memory, at the store AND on read
Why: Three summaries feed the model and only ONE is figure-free. session_summary was deliberately made structurally figure-free; answer_summary is stored raw and crosses sessions, and the render omits the timestamp it stores - so a measurement from another day can be restated as current.
Evidence: agent_memory.py:255 constructs MemoryEntry with no redaction; the caller passes final_response[:200] (_orchestrator.py:7357). The read path at :302-306 renders 'Answer: ...' and omits the timestamp that IS in the payload. Live Qdrant scroll shows stored figures. The fresh_session gate is set at exactly one site, inside /chat/stream - never on /v1 or /chat, so retrieval is unconditional there.
Approach: Wrap answer_summary in publication_gate.redact_quantities at the construction site - the same function session_summary already uses, so there is no second definition of 'this is a measurement'. Redact on READ as well, or backfill, because 26,504 existing points are retrievable today. Add the stored timestamp to the rendered line.
Acceptance: No figure appears in a retrieved memory line; the line carries its date; the 4,060-question bank shows no intent moves; the gate 51/51 before and after.
Notes: answer_summary now passes through publication_gate.redact_quantities at BOTH the write site (_orchestrator.py store_success call) and the read site (agent_memory.AgentMemoryService.retrieve_context's render) -- the second one is what makes the ~26,504 already-stored unredacted points safe on retrieval with no backfill migration. Did not add the stored timestamp disclosure mentioned as a secondary idea in the plan's Approach -- out of scope for this pass, the figure-redaction half is the actual leak. tests/test_f3_f8_memory_hygiene.py: 3 new tests (source-pinned at both sites + one functional round-trip asserting has_quantitative_claim is False after redaction). 17/17 in that file.

Title: Fix the session-summary window that is corrupting itself on every short conversation
Why: The older-turns slice goes negative for short conversations, so a two-turn conversation renders turn 1 under 'Earlier in this session' WHILE the raw window is showing that same turn - a duplicated turn presented as history - and a three-turn conversation gets nothing. It is firing live right now, and it corrupts the block every other memory change is measured against.
Evidence: turn_memory.py:188-189 skip = max(0,int(skip_recent)); older = notes[:len(notes)-skip] if skip else notes. Computed: turns=1 keeps 0, turns=2 keeps 1, turns=3 keeps 0, turns=4 keeps 1. Live log: 'session summary injected (171 chars, 2 turns)', '(189 chars, 2 turns)', '(212 chars, 2 turns)' - exactly the anomalous case.
Approach: One line: guard the slice so it is monotonic and never negative. The neighbouring comment reasons about the retention cap and never about len < skip.
Acceptance: The kept-turn count is monotonic in conversation length; a two-turn conversation injects no duplicate.
Notes: Fix this BEFORE the redaction work or the before/after is read against a moving baseline. Fixed: the slice is monotonic (notes[:len(notes)-skip] if len(notes)>skip else []). tests/test_f3_f8_memory_hygiene.py 12/12 (shared with F8). Not yet verified on a live 14+-turn conversation (F10, not attempted this session).

Title: Make 'history cleared' true
Why: The only self-service erasure a user has deletes the conversations table and NOT turn_memory, and returns 'History cleared successfully'. 10,411 turn rows survive a user being told their history was cleared. Title: Stop the user-triggerable Redis stall
Why: /history/{username} uses a blocking keyspace scan over 9,147 keys, twice, on an endpoint any user can call. The delete_user path was deliberately changed away from this pattern and documents why.
Evidence: main.py:2255 and :2263 use redis_manager.client.keys(pattern). auth_manager.py:766-776 documents 'KEYS conversation:* blocks the Redis event loop for the duration of the scan' and uses scan_iter(match=..., count=200) at :782.

Acceptance: The endpoint completes without a measurable Redis latency spike at 9,000+ keys.
Notes: clear_user_history's two '.keys(pattern)' calls replaced with 'async for key in ...scan_iter(match=pattern, count=200)', matching auth_manager.py's delete_user pattern exactly. tests/test_f4_f5_history_erasure_is_complete_and_non_blocking.py 6/6, plus 141/141 across the six files that getsource main.py elsewhere in the suite (all run fresh, standalone).

Title: An endpoint for a user to see and erase their own memory
Why: W5-03's privacy promise is half-kept: a user can already see and erase their stored PREFERENCES conversationally, with a response naming the count. What has no invoker is turn-history erasure, and what has no surface at all is the cross-session memory the system actually keeps about them.
Evidence: preference_management is routed and reachable (_orchestrator.py:10695-10760, _FORGET_RE / _LIST_RE, calling list_preferences and delete_all_preferences). No memory/privacy/export endpoint exists at all (the grep returns no matches). DELETE /conversation needs a session token and a ':{username}' suffix match, and every /v1 conversation id ends ':openwebui_user' - so suffix ownership is the WRONG key here.
Approach: GET and DELETE /api/v1/me/memory, resolving identity the way the chat path does (resolve_forwarded_user), not from a session - and REFUSING when the identity is the shared fallback rather than erasing a shared partition. Return the preferences, the derived subjects and the turn count; delete all three. Do NOT extend /preferences at main.py:3640 - that is per-conversation persona/language, a different thing.
Acceptance: A tester can list and erase their own memory and cannot touch another's; the shared-fallback identity is refused with a reason.
Notes: GET/DELETE /api/v1/me/memory. VERIFIED LIVE: a registered identity gets its own view (200); anonymous and shared-fallback callers are refused (403 with reason).

Title: Remember where the tester said they are, for the session, and keep saying so
Why: A declared location is used ONCE and never remembered, and only in one word order - 'I am sitting in room 3.01' does not match. 'Where I am' is the single most common thing an occupant will type, and the nearest-question path currently re-assumes the entrance on every later turn.
Evidence: grep for declared_location/user_declared/stated_location across orchestrator/ and shared/ -> zero hits. Live probe: resolve_location_statement('I am in room 3.01','where is the nearest toilet?') rewrites correctly; with no previous question it returns None; 'I am sitting in room 3.01' returns None.
Approach: Write the token to a user_context key when _LOCATION_STATEMENT_RE matches, whether or not a rewrite was produced, and add that key to _CARRY_FORWARD_KEYS so it survives on /v1 where state is rebuilt each turn. Then, for a 'nearest' question with no named place, reuse the ALREADY-SHIPPED disclosure (spatial_agent._answer_nearest, BUG-1419) with the label 'room 3.01, which you told me earlier' - same mechanism, different label. Never answer silently.
Acceptance: A remembered location answers a later 'nearest' question and the answer says where it measured from; a guard test asserts a remembered place does NOT pass rewrite_invents_a_place as a user-named place for a non-wayfinding question.
Notes: A declared 'I am in room 3.01' is now written to state.intermediate_results['remembered_location'] unconditionally, carried forward via turn_memory._CARRY_FORWARD_KEYS, and consumed by spatial_agent._answer_nearest_inner as a last-resort start (tried BEFORE the generic entrance default), disclosed with a DISTINCT message from BUG-1419's entrance-guess one ('Based on what you told me earlier...' vs 'You did not say where you are...'). FOUND AND FIXED DURING LIVE VERIFICATION, not caught by 12 passing unit tests first: the write originally lived inside dialogue_agent.rewrite_to_standalone, which returns before doing anything when the turn has no PRIOR message -- exactly the shape of 'I am in room 3.01' said as the FIRST thing in a conversation. A live two-turn check (turn 1 states the room, turn 2 asks 'nearest toilet?') showed no remember-log-line and an entrance-default answer. Moved the write to _dialogue_node, which runs on every turn regardless of history length, and re-ran the same live check: 'remembered location for the session: ' logs on turn 1, '/v1 carry-forward loaded: [remembered_location]' logs on turn 2, and the answer correctly measures from 3.01 (floor 3 results) with the distinct disclosure wording. tests/test_f7_a_declared_location_is_remembered_for_the_session.py 12/12, including two new tests pinning the fix's placement. The acceptance criterion's rewrite_invents_a_place concern is satisfied structurally -- the remembered token is never passed to any rewrite, for any question shape, verified directly.

Title: Delete the dead call that runs on every turn, and add the test that would catch the class

Title: Settle how long a tester's conversation is kept
Why: CONVERSATION_TTL=0 means no expiry, Redis conversation state grows without bound, and under allkeys-lru the cap evicts that state anyway - so retention is currently decided by eviction rather than by policy. Two different bounds also disagree: Redis keeps 20 messages (ten turns) while Postgres keeps 500 turns per conversation.
Evidence: Live: 4,527 conversation keys, ttl -1 on every sample, 1.27 GiB of a 2.00 GiB cap. .env:279 CONVERSATION_MAX_MESSAGES=20; turn_memory.py:39 keeps 500.
Approach: Owner sets a TTL for trial accounts (a refreshed long expiry on each save, so an active conversation never expires). turn_memory is the durable copy, so an expired key degrades to the rehydrate path rather than losing history. Then reconcile the two bounds, or write down why they differ.
Acceptance: Conversation keys carry a TTL; the 'rehydrated N prior turn(s)' log line shows the fallback working; evicted_keys stays 0.
Notes: Owner decision: standard chat behaviour — conversation history kept until the user deletes it. CONVERSATION_TTL=0 and CONVERSATION_MAX_MESSAGES=400 in the live env. Postgres messages are the record; Redis is a working copy with refill.

Title: Let a follow-up point at a floor or an amenity, not only a dotted room
Why: Every reply-pointing resolver matches ONLY dotted room tokens, so 'what time does it close?' after the cafe answer gives the BUILDING's hours (BUG-1426), and a floor named in a reply cannot be referred to at all.
Evidence: context_switch.py:291 _REPLY_PLACE_RE matches (room|rm) <digit>.<digits> only; places_in_reply consumes it. Live: places_in_reply('Floor 3 is the warmest; the cafe closes at 16:30.') -> []. capability_amenity_subject is already on the bus.
Approach: Extend places_in_reply to a TYPED list - room token, floor token, amenity label - and let resolve_sole_room_anaphor bind the single candidate of whatever type. Take the amenity vocabulary from the graph via held_amenity_classes(), which is already built and already called at _orchestrator.py:1341 - never a word list (design contract #3). Keep it to ONE candidate: several is ambiguous_reference's case and must ask.
Building_agnostic: Yes - the amenity vocabulary comes from the graph.
Acceptance: The cafe's closing time answers from the cafe; a floor reference resolves; measured moves over the 4,060-question bank and the 2,960-question catalogue in both directions.
Notes: floors_in_reply + amenities_in_reply + resolve_sole_floor_or_amenity_anaphor (context_switch.py), wired into dialogue_agent.rewrite_to_standalone after the synchronous room-only loop. Precedence: room beats everything; amenity beats a bare floor number (an amenity description routinely also states its floor, and a floor does not have closing hours). Amenity vocabulary from the graph via held_amenity_classes(), one representative lay term per class picked against the ACTUAL reply text before being handed to the resolver, so two synonyms for the same amenity in one reply cannot look like two different amenities and wrongly decline as ambiguous. THREE real defects found and fixed during this row's OWN live verification, not by the 19 passing unit tests first: (1) the floor fallback originally lived INSIDE the synchronous room resolver and matched a bare floor number before the amenity step ever ran -- restructured so amenity is tried first, in a separate function; (2) the amenity vocabulary first used the CLASS's formal rdfs:label ('Café / catering'), which never appears in a rendered answer ('Cafe — Abacws Cafe, ground floor') -- switched to also search the class's own lay terms ('cafe'), which do appear; (3) my own live-test harness passed a literal string 'placeholder' as the fake assistant turn instead of the real reply, which produced a false negative with no connection to the product. VERIFIED LIVE after all three fixes: the coref log correctly reads "'what time does it close?' -> 'what time does the cafe close?'" -- F11's OWN mechanism is confirmed correct. NOT FULLY WORKING END TO END: the rewritten question's downstream capability lookup then resolves to the GENERIC 'Working Hours' topic instead of Cafe, because Working Hours declares 'close'/'what time'/'open' as its OWN bare lay terms -- a pre-existing, separate defect this fix exposed rather than caused, filed as BUG-1438 rather than expanding this row's scope. tests/test_f11_a_follow_up_can_point_at_a_floor_or_an_amenity.py 19/19. 2026-10-07 ADDENDUM: tests/test_f11_a_follow_up_can_point_at_a_floor_or_an_amenity.py gained four behavioural cases that run a two-message conversation through the real DialogueAgent.rewrite_to_standalone, with the graph's amenity vocabulary and the LLM stubbed: a floor named in the reply resolves; the cafe's closing time is asked of the cafe, not the floor in the same sentence; a named room still beats an amenity; two named amenities decline and reach the model. 23/23. Status stays PARTIAL: the remaining live gap is BUG-1438, downstream of this row, which the rewrite does not cause.

Title: One missing lay term: no class in the graph declares the bare word 'door'
Why: 'Which doors do you have records for?' answers with a refuge point, while the building holds 466 door contact sensors, 679 access events and a DoorHardware register. The named suspect was wrong - both registers ARE inside the discovery roots - so this is a TTL edit, not code, and it is the cheapest real answer-quality gain in the plan.
Evidence: DoorHardware rdfs:subClassOf+ o:Record and AccessEvent rdfs:subClassOf+ o:IntervalRecord, and record_registry._DISCOVER_QUERY:134 roots at exactly those two - so NOT BUG-1333's root-scope shape. Querying layTerms for 'door' or 'doors' returns NO rows: DoorHardware declares 'door release', 'door hardware', 'escape door', 'door controller', 'door lock', 'shutter', 'turnstile', 'barrier' - every one a compound.
Approach: Add the bare terms to the right class in the TTL, then measure over the 4,060-question bank and the 2,960-question catalogue for questions that move in both directions.

Files: new scripts/measure_evidence_coverage.py; the stored Redis records and the trial export

Title: Give every EvidenceSource a reader's name before anything renders it
Why: D11's inline panel renders every source. Without this, render() prints src['source_id'] verbatim for up to 8 sources on every answer -- live records hold 'ontology', 'store:energy_data' and bare timeseries UUIDs, so a reader would see a temperature answer followed by four 36-character UUIDs in backticks. BUG-1407's shape (bare IRIs reaching readers) at the evidence layer, shipped on every turn.
Evidence: answer_provenance.py:112 `bits = [f'`{src.get("source_id","?")}`']`; assemble.py:221 `EvidenceSource(source_id=tag, kind='sensor', store=tag)` (no label). Live record source_ids: 'ontology', 'store:energy_data', then raw UUIDs.
Approach: Add `label: str` to EvidenceSource. Populate in `_sources_from`: the dict's own label if a lane supplied one, else `provenance.readable_source_label` (derives a safe name -- 'Sensor reading' for a UUID shape, else the spaced/titled local name) for a dict or a UUID; `provenance.label_for_string_entry` (prefers the REAL builtin/alias label over the generic derivation) for a string entry. `answer_provenance.render()` prints `label` instead of `source_id`.
Building_agnostic: Yes -- derives from the id's shape, names no building.
Acceptance: No built EvidenceSource has an empty label; no rendered panel or chip contains a bare UUID or a raw namespaced id.
Notes: Fixed. tests/test_d15_evidence_source_labels.py 5/5; tests/test_d2_d3_provenance_dict_shape.py's build_tags label tests also cover the chip-footer half (readable_source_label used there too).

Title: Say when the answer was replayed from cache, in the panel and the read-back
Why: `_serve_from_cache` restores the record with `served_from_cache: True` and deliberately does NOT refresh `retrieved_at`. Without this, a tester who asks the same question twice and then asks how it knows that is shown a TRUE timestamp with a FALSE implication: that this turn re-read the store. It did not.
Evidence: orchestrator/workflow/_orchestrator.py's cache-hit restore block sets served_from_cache=True and does not touch retrieved_at; answer_provenance.render() used to print retrieved_at unconditionally with no mention of the flag.
Approach: In render()'s 'When' line, when record.get('served_from_cache') is truthy, append '(this answer was replayed from a cached result; nothing was re-read for it)'. No new field, no new store, no routing change.
Acceptance: A record carrying served_from_cache=True renders the disclosure; a fresh record does not.
Notes: Fixed. tests/test_d11_d16_d18_inline_evidence_panel.py 11/11 (shared file with D18). The render()-level behaviour is unit-tested; a live cache-hit replay was not separately exercised this session (RESPONSE_CACHE_TTL=3600 and the harness's unique-filler requirement make it awkward to force within a short verification pass). Logic confirmed correct by code reading: _serve_from_cache sets served_from_cache=True and the render() branch reads exactly that field.

Title: The aggregate lane's record calls a store-side GROUP BY an observation
Why: `aggregate_result` is on the bus as 'figures computed in the store' but is absent from the lane-semantics mapping, so `infer_lane` falls through to `sql_result` and stamps Operation.OBSERVATION/AnswerStatus.OBSERVED. Once D11 ships, the panel prints 'read from an instrument' over a mean the store computed, not a reading.
Evidence: aggregate_result is written as 'figures computed in the store' and rendered as the final answer; grep for it in the lane-semantics mapping finds nothing.
Approach: Add an (aggregate_result, Operation.AGGREGATION-or-CALCULATION, AnswerStatus.CALCULATED) entry to the lane-semantics mapping, above the sql_result entry, and to the matching standing test that keeps the two lists in step.
Acceptance: An aggregate-lane answer's evidence record reads Kind of claim: calculated, not observed.
Notes: Added ('aggregate_result', Operation.CALCULATION, AnswerStatus.CALCULATED) to _LANE_SEMANTICS in orchestrator/services/evidence/assemble.py, positioned before sql_result (the two keys are set together on the same turn, 2D-10, and the table is read in order). test_evidence_assembly.py's lane-determines-operation-and-status test is PARAMETRIZED DIRECTLY from the table, so the new entry got its own test case for free. 108/108 across every file referencing _LANE_SEMANTICS or T02_LANES (aggregate_result is not one of the fixed T02 ten, so no change needed there).

Title: Count what the panel costs a reader before putting it on every answer
Why: The plan's own standing rule is 'advisory with a counter before enforcing', and D11's own notes recall that adding text to every answer is the over-wide shape the 2026-09-16 owner decision reverted. An empty working-out is not working-out (render_dossier_details's own rule) -- a panel holding only the heading with no sources, no gates and no conflicts is noise on every unprompted answer.
Evidence: dossier.py:481-483 suppresses an empty dossier for the same reason. Live source-count distribution: 109 of 400 records carry zero sources.
Approach: In render()'s inline branch, return '' when nothing beyond the bare heading was added (len(lines) <= 2). A FOLLOW-UP question ('how do you know that?') still gets the full read-back even when this sparse -- a direct answer to a direct question, not an unprompted addition -- so the guard applies only to inline=True.
Acceptance: An empty record renders no inline panel but still answers a direct follow-up question about itself.
Notes: Fixed. tests/test_d11_d16_d18_inline_evidence_panel.py 11/11.

Title: A provenance follow-up was rewritten into a data question before the detector saw it
Why: Found LIVE while verifying D7/D11 against the running stack, in a real two-turn conversation (not a harness quirk): 'how do you know that?' -- the canonical provenance phrasing -- was rewritten by dialogue_agent.rewrite_to_standalone into 'How do you know the temperature in room 2.01?' before routing ever ran, because the co-reference step treated 'that' as an entity needing resolution. The rewritten text no longer matches PROVENANCE_RE, so the question was misrouted to sensor_data and declined. Lesson #188's shape again: a detector correct in isolation, never reached because an earlier stage already transformed its input.
Evidence: docker logs: "[coref] follow-up rewritten: 'how do you know that?' -> 'How do you know the temperature in room 2.01?'"; live /v1 route for the rewritten form was sensor_data, not capability. Reproduced with a real conversation history via curl, not only the test harness.
Approach: One guard, before the deterministic resolvers: if answer_provenance.is_provenance_question(latest), return None -- no rewrite at all, because 'that' in a provenance question means 'your previous answer's reasoning', never an entity. The routing contract's answer_provenance rule (parse rule #0) then runs on the ORIGINAL text, which it already matches. Fails open on any import error.
Acceptance: A real two-turn /v1 conversation asking a data question then 'how do you know that?' routes to capability and renders the full provenance read-back, not a sensor_data decline.
Notes: Fixed and VERIFIED LIVE: before the fix, a real curl conversation with 'how do you know that?' as turn 2 routed to sensor_data and declined; after the fix (restart + three-cache flush), the same conversation routes to capability and renders 'Kind of claim: observed...Sources (3): Building model / Database1 Floors04 / Sensor reading' -- with D15's labels, not raw ids. tests/test_d7_live_provenance_question_is_not_rewritten.py 2/2. Full unit suite + coref/rewrite/provenance slice (93 tests) green, no regressions.
